object_description: compact seven-story atrium volume with roof pergola
design_condition: Placed on the northeastern edge of the plot and kept below the surrounding height horizon, the compact volume frees generous street-facing outdoor spaces and forms a raised piazza while leaving a weaker western connection.

positive.statement: The compact volume remains below the maximum height and lies within the horizon of the surrounding campus buildings.
The reduced footprint creates high-quality outdoor spaces framed by plane trees.
The ground-floor uses and open-space design are well coordinated, including deliveries.
The raised piazza is ideal as a meeting point and observation post.
The open framework gives the building an institutional character, with a balanced tension between rawness and noblesse.
The building is clearly structured, and the generous vestibule separates school and sports use.
The atrium acts as the heart of the building, combining architectural, functional, spatial, and building-technology requirements while giving identity to the pragmatic room configuration.
The project implements the spatial program in an extremely space-efficient manner and conserves resources.
The building technology concept appears well thought out and innovative.
The atrium provides good lighting for the interior rooms and supports night cooling.
The supporting structure allows spatial adjustments in both directions.

negative.statement: The massing of bicycles next to the building entrance feels cramped.
The lack of western access would have anchored the building better in the urban fabric.
The nodes of the diagonal struts are shown too glossily, and the edge beams of the facade are too low.
It is unclear how exhaust air is routed.
The arrival area is under too much pressure, and the student flows are not meaningfully unbundled.
The corridor widths seem implausible, and the spiral staircase may not accommodate the large number of students.
Under these conditions, smooth school operations hardly seem possible.
The atrium type is not stated, and a sprinkler and fire-alarm system will presumably be necessary.
